summary: Layer 2 Tunneling Protocol version 3 can tunnel a variety of data link protocols over IP networks. This document describes the specifics of tunneling High-Level Data Link Control (HDLC) frames over L2TPv3. It is standards-track and was updated by RFC 5641.

eli5.summary: It takes messages from an old kind of wire, carries them inside the internet, and sets them back down at the other end as if the wire never broke.

questions: how to tunnel hdlc frames over ip
how are hdlc frames tunneled over ip
what is the l2tpv3 circuit status avp
subtitle: How to carry HDLC frames across an IP network as an L2TPv3 pseudowire, including link status signalling.

tldr.problem: Serial links that use HDLC framing need to be connected across an IP network as if the link were a single wire.
tldr.mechanism: Each HDLC interface is paired with an L2TPv3 session of pseudowire type 0x0006; frames lose their flags and FCS and cross the tunnel, and the Circuit Status AVP in Set Link Info messages reports whether the link is up.
tldr.outcome: Anything with HDLC-like framing, such as PPP, Frame Relay or X.25 (LAPB), can cross the tunnel, with the endpoints taking no part in those protocols. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and was later updated by RFC 5641.

today: RFC 4349 is a Proposed Standard published in February 2006 and has not been obsoleted, but it was updated by RFC 5641. It builds on the base L2TPv3 protocol in RFC 3931.

sections.title: HDLC Pseudowires over L2TPv3
sections.content:
RFC 3931 defines the base protocol for Layer 2 tunneling over IP networks (L2TPv3). This document adds the specifics for tunneling HDLC frames. The emulated circuits are called HDLC Pseudowires (HDLCPWs).

It covers simple point-to-point frame encapsulation, for example between two L2TPv3 nodes, and simple interface up and interface down notifications. Readers are expected to be very familiar with the terminology of RFC 3931.
sections.eli5: An old kind of wire is being pretended over the internet. This document says how to pack the wire's messages into internet packets and how to tell the far end when the wire goes up or down.

sections.title: Control Connection and Session Setup
sections.content:
First, an L2TPv3 control connection MUST be established. The SCCRQ and SCCRP messages MUST include the HDLC Pseudowire Type 0x0006 in the Pseudowire Capabilities List, marking the connection as able to carry HDLCPWs. Each LCCE (L2TP Control Connection Endpoint) MUST identify itself by a globally unique value, by default in the Router ID AVP, though the Hostname AVP MAY be used.

When an HDLC interface is provisioned and becomes ACTIVE, an L2TP session is set up with the standard three-way handshake: ICRQ, ICRP and ICCN. An LCCE MAY start the session right after provisioning, or wait until the interface is ACTIVE, which delays resource allocation until needed. The Pseudowire Type AVP (Attribute Type 68) MUST be in the ICRQ with value 0x0006, the Circuit Status AVP MUST be in the ICRQ and ICRP, and the Remote End ID AVP MUST be in the ICRQ. At a minimum, an unstructured four-octet value known to both ends must be supported.

If the far end has not provisioned the interface, it answers with a CDN, and the initiator SHOULD retry periodically, with a configurable period and retry count. If a link is removed at either end, the session MUST be torn down with a CDN carrying one of two new result codes: 20 (link deleted permanently) or 21 (link INACTIVE for an extended period).
sections.eli5: Two routers first agree they can carry this kind of wire. Then, when each end of the wire is ready, they swap three short messages, like a handshake, and start passing data.

sections.title: Link Status Notification and Keepalive
sections.content:
Once a session is up, the Set Link Info (SLI) control message signals changes in the HDLC link status between the two ends. An SLI MUST be sent any time a value in the Circuit Status AVP changes. The initial ICRQ, ICRP and CDN messages are the exceptions, since they set up and tear down the session itself.

An implementation MAY send an ICRQ or ICRP before its interface is ACTIVE, as long as the Circuit Status AVP says INACTIVE and an SLI is sent when it becomes ACTIVE.

All sessions on a control connection use the L2TP Hello facility for keepalive, which gives basic dead peer and path detection between the endpoints.
sections.eli5: If the wire goes dead at one end, that end sends a short note to the other. Both ends also say hello now and then to check the other is still there.

sections.title: The Circuit Status AVP
sections.content:
HDLC reports link state with the Circuit Status AVP from RFC 3931, Attribute Type 71. Its value is a 16-bit mask in which only the two least significant bits are defined. Reserved bits MUST be set to 0 when sending and ignored on receipt.

The N (New) bit SHOULD be 1 if the indication is for a new HDLC circuit, and 0 otherwise. The A (Active) bit is 1 when the interface is ACTIVE and 0 when INACTIVE. In the example exchange in the RFC, an active new link is reported as status 0x03.
sections.eli5: It is a tiny card with two checkboxes: is this a brand-new wire, and is it working right now?

sections.title: Encapsulation, Sequencing and MTU
sections.content:
HDLCPWs use the default L2TPv3 encapsulations for demultiplexing, sequencing and flags, in an interface-to-interface fashion. The HDLC PDU is stripped of flags and the trailing FCS, bit or byte unstuffing is performed, and the rest (address, control and protocol fields included) crosses the pseudowire. Because it is transparent, any protocol with HDLC-like framing can use it, including PPP, Frame Relay and X.25 (LAPB). The negotiations of those protocols, such as PPP's LCP or Frame Relay's LMI, happen between the remote systems, and the LCCEs do not take part. Modes that need the flags, FCS or unstuffing, such as PPP ACCM negotiation, are exceptions.

Data packet sequencing MAY be enabled, using the L2TPv3 mechanisms; when it is enabled, HDLCPWs MUST request the Default L2-Specific Sublayer.

Encapsulation makes the packet N bytes longer than the HDLC frame without flags or FCS. N is 4 to 16 octets when L2TPv3 runs directly over IP, and 16 to 28 octets when over UDP, not counting the IP header. It depends on the session header (Session ID is 4 octets, the Cookie is 0, 4 or 8 octets, and over UDP there are 4 more octets of flags and version) and the optional 4-octet sublayer used for sequencing.
sections.eli5: The pseudowire takes the letter out of its envelope, ships just the letter, and puts it into a fresh envelope at the far end. The extra shipping box makes each parcel a little bigger.

sections.title: Applicability Statement
sections.content:
HDLCPWs are for point-to-point, port-to-port deployment. Compared with the native service, a few things differ. The FCS is stripped at the ingress endpoint and regenerated at the egress endpoint, so it may not reflect errors on the end-to-end link, and corruption in transit may go undetected. That may not matter if the inner protocols check integrity themselves; otherwise the session can use IPsec as described in RFC 3931.

The packet-switched network may reorder, duplicate or silently drop packets, and sequencing can be enabled to detect this per session. The faithfulness of a pseudowire may also be improved by using Quality of Service features of the endpoints and the network.
sections.eli5: Because the little check number is thrown away and made again at the other end, a smudge in the middle might not be noticed, unless the things inside check themselves or you lock the box with IPsec.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: HDLC over L2TPv3 is subject to the security considerations in RFC 3931. Beyond those that apply when carrying other data link types, the RFC states that there are no additional considerations specific to carrying HDLC.
sections.eli5: The same safety rules as the main tunnel apply, and carrying this kind of wire adds no new ones.

messages.label: ICRP (status = 0x03)
messages.note: Sent once B's interface is ACTIVE.

messages.label: ICCN
messages.note: Session established; OK to send data into the tunnel.

fields.name: Reserved
fields.desc: Reserved for future use; set to 0 when sending, ignored on receipt.

fields.name: N
fields.desc: New: 1 if the indication is for a new HDLC circuit.

fields.name: A
fields.desc: Active: 1 if the interface is ACTIVE, 0 if INACTIVE.
